subject: Marketplace listing gating questions + rev-share / metering exceptions
messages:
From: CloudBridge Sales <sales@cloudbridge.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 16:46:00 -0700
Subject: Intro + listing requirements for CloudBridge-Redwood bundle

Hi Soojin,

Great to meet on the call earlier. Quick follow-up from our product/partner team — we have a draft marketplace listing and a few asks to align on before we push to AWS/GCP catalogs:

- Rev-share tiers: CloudBridge assumes standard 85/15 (publisher/partner) unless otherwise negotiated.
- Metering: we plan to report usage via a custom SKU (tokens-based). Need confirmation on how Redwood maps token units to your metering.
- Co-sell evidence: sample architecture diagram and security questionnaire (SOC2) — we will drop those into your Drive.

If you can point us to the correct legal or partner ops contacts and flag any immediate redlines for the rev-share or metering approach, we can prepare a clean DocuSign for partner acceptance.

Attachments: architecture-overview.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Ravi Shah
Head of Partnerships, CloudBridge
Ravi Shah <sales@cloudbridge.io>

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: CloudBridge Sales <sales@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + listing requirements for CloudBridge-Redwood bundle

Ravi — thanks for the summary and the deck. Happy to own the listing coordination from our side. A few pragmatic notes up front so we avoid rework: 

1) Rev-share: our standard marketplace operating model varies by cloud. For AWS we typically accept publisher-facing splits but pass-throughs require an MCN/legal check. Ben (cc) is our channel lead and will confirm the allowed ranges.

2) Metering / SKU mapping: we prefer to map cloud metering to a normalized "inference-unit" (tokens * token-weight). Alex can share a short spec. If CloudBridge requires a custom SKU, that’s OK but there are additional listing/regulatory steps.

3) Evidence & legal: Karthik (legal) — any clauses you want us to pre-clear (SLA credits, refund language, data residency exceptions)? If CloudBridge needs a non-standard SLA addendum, please send a proposed draft and we’ll route to legal for redlines.

Next steps:
- Ravi: drop the SOC2 and architecture artifacts into the Drive link you mentioned.
- Ben: can you confirm whether the 85/15 is acceptable for AWS listing or if we need to escalate?
- Karthik: flag any agreement language to triage.

I’ll start an internal listing checklist and share it once we have the metering spec.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Head of Alliances — Redwood Inference
[attachment: listing-intake-template.csv]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, CloudBridge Sales <sales@cloudbridge.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + listing requirements for CloudBridge-Redwood bundle

Soojin / Ravi — quick note on rev-share and go-to-market credits:

- 85/15 as a headline is acceptable for a co-sell engagement, but for AWS Marketplace there are two considerations: (1) whether CloudBridge will be the publisher or Redwood will list a bundled offering; (2) if a reseller flow is used there are different payout timelines.
- We can accept 85/15 if CloudBridge agrees to be the primary publisher for AWS and signs the co-sell commitment form. Otherwise, if Redwood publishes, we need to discuss compensation for sales credits.

On metering: please share a sample of expected token volumes and pricing bands. If you expect spiky enterprise usage, recommend a tiered SKU (light/standard/heavy) to keep costs predictable.

I’ll coordinate with GTM to map the crediting model once legal confirms the publishing flow.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Channel GTM, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, CloudBridge Sales <sales@cloudbridge.io>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + listing requirements for CloudBridge-Redwood bundle

Team — putting legal/ops asks in one place. I attached a short addendum we’d like to propose for any non-standard SLA/rev-share exceptions. Key points:

- Co-Sell Crediting: define GTM crediting trigger events (demo, pipeline lead, closed-won) and associated % credit.
- Refund/SLA credits: cap credits to a monthly maximum tied to committed capacity.
- Metering reconciliation: monthly reporting cadence, CSV schema, and dispute window (30 days).
- Data residency: if CloudBridge requires EU-only nodes we need commitment on traffic routing and potential surcharge.

Please see attached: CoSell_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf (stub) and a short metering workbook (metering-exceptions-summary.xlsx).

Ravi — if these points look OK, we can prepare a DocuSign with the sections to agree on. If you anticipate additional commercial asks (upfront credits, market dev funds), call them out now.

Karthik
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: CoSell_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf]
[attachment: metering-exceptions-summary.xlsx]

From: CloudBridge Sales <sales@cloudbridge.io>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + listing requirements for CloudBridge-Redwood bundle

Thanks all — the addendum looks reasonable overall. A couple of clarifications before we sign: 

- Metering reconciliation: CloudBridge requests a 45-day dispute window instead of 30 on initial launch while our reporting pipeline stabilizes.
- Co-sell credits: we would like the demo->pipeline credit to be 40% for the first 90 days as an introductory incentive.

I’ve uploaded the SOC2 and architecture to your Drive folder and started the DocuSign envelope with the addendum (link below). Please let me know if Redwood can accept the modified dispute window and the temporary demo credit uplift.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/DocuSign/Envelope12345
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleCoSellEvidence

If those two items are the only exceptions, happy to sign and proceed with the AWS listing intake.

—Ravi
